description_en: Aśikharatemple from circa 13th-15th century at the Bhurtī Temple Complex.The monument is the southernmostśikharatemple of the Bhurtī Temple Complex. The site itself is located in the northern end of the settlement of Bhurtī, 3 km north of Narayana, the district headquarters. It currently comprises 22 standingśikharatemples (ordevala) and one stone fountain. Architectural activity at the site can be situated between the 13thand 15thcentury, a time period corresponding to the latter part of the Khaśa Malla empire and the early phase of the Rāskoṭi dynasty (Andolfatto 2019,Pokharel 2011: 128-129,Sharma 1972: 23-31,Sharma 2012: 120-123).The monument is built on an individual stone platform. It is oriented to the south, as for most of the temples at the site. The sanctum is currently empty. The top part of the temple, which is traditionally surmounted by twoāmalakarings, now has a single ring, of recent origin. According to local informants the work was supervised by the Department of Archaeology and executed by stone sculptors from Bhaktapur.In 2008, the “Bhurti Temple Complex of Dailekh” was included in UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List.
monument_assessment: Restored, Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
